data.subject: NYSE - Fee Changes Effective November 2026
data.body:

The monthly free volume threshold for Late D Orders will increase to 15,000,000 shares, up from 10,000,000, for qualifying member organizations. Rates for volume above the threshold remain unchanged. For additional details, please click here.

Reminder: Register for the new NYSE Research subscription at www.nyse.com/subscriptions to receive updates when new research articles are published. The subscription includes all NYSE research and thought leadership content, which is available at www.nyse.com/research/insights.

Please contact rmteam@nyse.com with any questions about these updates.

data.subject: NYSE American Options: SPY Binary Return Options Available October 29
data.body:
On October 29, 2026, NYSE American Options will begin listing Binary Return Options on SPY (B1SPY). These European-style, all-or-nothing options pay a fixed $100 at expiration if the underlying security closes at or above the strike for a Finish High (call) option, or below the strike for a Finish Low (put) option, and $0 otherwise. Settlement is based on the closing price reported by the underlying security's primary listing market. 

Binary Return Options are available for testing in the Certification environment. Please contact tms@nyse.com to test. 

For additional details, refer to the Binary Return Options: Product Overview. Please contact rmteam@nyse.com with any questions about this update.

data.subject: NYSE American Options: Binary Return Options
data.body:
NYSE American Options will make Binary Return Options eligible for listing on October 26, 2026, pending effectiveness of a regulatory filing. These options offer an all-or-nothing outcome at expiration, determined by the closing price of the underlying security as reported by its primary listing market.

Binary Return Options are available for testing in the Exchange's Certification environment. To get started, please contact tms@nyse.com.

Product Snapshot:

  • European-style options that pay a fixed $100 at expiration if the underlying security closes on the correct side of the strike, and $0 otherwise
  • Finish High (call) pays out if the underlying closes at or above the strike; Finish Low (put) pays out if the underlying closes below the strike, so exactly one side pays out
  • Binary Return Options are automatically exercised under OCC rules
  • Five consecutive weekly expiration series, with new series added each Thursday
  • Twelve underlying securities initially, each with a distinct Binary Return symbol (e.g. B1SPY)
  • Penny quoting and trading during the Core Trading Session, 9:30 a.m. to 4:00 p.m. ET (4:15 p.m. for eligible ETPs)
  • New SeriesType field value of '4' = (Binary) in certain market data messages

For additional details, review the product Binary Return Options: Product Overview.  Please contact rmteam@nyse.com with any questions.

data.subject: FINRA/NYSE TRF® - Extended Operating Hours Testing Schedule
data.body:
Effective December 6, 2026, FINRA/NYSE TRF® ("NYSE TRF") will extend its operating hours in alignment with the recently approved CTA and UTP Plan amendments to extend the operating hours of the Securities Information Processors pursuant to the proposed rule change to amend the FINRA Rule 6300 Series, as announced in a May FINRA Technical Notice and in a FINRA/NYSE TRF ® Trader Update in July 2026. 

NYSE TRF will operate from 9:00 p.m. ET Sunday through 8:00 p.m. ET Friday, with a one-hour pause between 8:00 p.m. and 9:00 p.m. ET Monday through Thursday, excluding holidays. This expands the current operating hours of 4:00 a.m. - 8:00 p.m. ET, Monday through Friday, excluding holidays. 

Extended Hours Trading Testing Schedule 

Certification testing will be available beginning October 2, 2026. 

FINRA/NYSE TRF® will conduct six tests ahead of the December 6 Production launch, in conjunction with the Securities Information Processors. Tests will begin at 11:00 p.m. ET on Friday and conclude at 12:00 p.m. ET on Saturday. 

The scheduled industry test dates are: 

  • October 2 | October 16 | October 30 | November 6 | November 20 | December 4 

Beginning November 8, 2026, test symbols will be available for Production testing during the Overnight Session.

data.subject: NYSE Options - Cash-Settled FLEX ETF Options Eligibility Update
data.body:
Overview 

FLEX ETF Options are eligible for cash settlement if the underlying ETF meets the following criteria based on a bi-annual review of the prior six-month period 

  • Average daily notional value of $500 million or more 
  • Consolidated average daily volume of 4,680,000 shares or more 

What's Changing 

  • The previous 50-ETF cap has been removed. 
  • Newly eligible ETFs may be added between reviews using a one-month lookback, provided they meet 20% higher thresholds: 
  • Average daily notional value of $600 million or more 
  • Consolidated average daily volume of 5,616,000 shares or more 
  • ETFs that no longer meet the eligibility thresholds following the bi-annual review may continue trading as cash-settled based on existing open interest.

data.subject: NYSE Options Introduces Intraday 1-minute Open-Close Volume Summary Products
data.body:
NYSE Options is pleased to announce the launch of the Intraday 1-minute Open-Close Volume Summary product on NYSE Arca Options and on NYSE American Options, beginning Thursday, October 1, 2026.

The Intraday 1-minute Open-Close Volume Summary provides aggregates of volume traded on the NYSE Options markets at the option level by

  • Origin (i.e., Customer, Professional Customer, Firm, Broker-Dealer, and Market Maker)
  • Buying/selling
  • Contract volume
  • Transaction type (opening/closing)

The Customer, Professional Customer, Firm, Broker-Dealer, and Market Maker volume is further broken down into trade size buckets (fewer than 100 contracts, 100-199 contracts, greater than 199 contracts), and files are captured every 1-minute throughout the trading day.

The Intraday 1-minute Open-Close Volume Summary is available for purchase on a monthly subscription basis and on an ad-hoc basis.*

NYSE Options Open-Close Volume Summary Product Specification is available here, and sample files are available here.

data.subject: NYSE Group - Market Wide Circuit Breaker Test September 12, 2026
data.body:
On Saturday, September 12, 2026, NYSE, NYSE American, NYSE Arca, NYSE National and NYSE Texas will participate in the Securities Information Processors' (SIPs) industry testing of Market-Wide Circuit Breaker (MWCB) Level 1 - 3. NYSE Group equities markets will be available from their primary data sites in Mahwah from 9:30 a.m. to 12:00 p.m. ET.  

Designated required participants for the October 2026 Reg. SCI test on NYSE, NYSE American, NYSE Arca, NYSE National and NYSE Texas are required to participate in at least one MWCB test, per year.  Firms required to test have been notified of their requirement.  

The script for the test can be found here. The testing requirements below must be completed for each NYSE Group equities exchange for which the firm has been designated as a required tester:

  • Receive and process MWCB halt messages from the SIPs.  
  • Receive and process resume messages from the SIPs following a MWCB halt.  
  • Receive and process market data from the SIPs relevant to the MWCB halt.  
  • Send orders following a Level 1 or Level 2 MWCB halt in a manner consistent with usual trading behavior.  

Firms should register to test at trading@nyse.com to have their participation recorded. Following the test, firms must return the participation checklist to Regscitesting@nyse.com.

Remaining 2026 SIP Failover/MWCB Saturday Testing Dates 

  • September 12, 2026 - MWCB Level 1/2/3 Test   
  • December 5, 2026 - SIP Failover / MWCB Level 1/2 Test #3

data.subject: NYSE Options: Professional Customer Order Review Period Update
data.body:
NYSE Arca Options and NYSE American Options have amended their respective 'Definitions - Customer and Professional Customer' rules (NYSE Arca Rule 1, NYSE American Rule 900.2NY) to require Member Firms to review customer activity on a monthly basis, rather than quarterly, to determine whether orders that are not for the account of a Broker or Dealer should be represented as Professional Customer orders.

Orders for any non-Broker/Dealer customer that had an average of more than 390 orders per day during a calendar month must be represented as Professional Customer orders for the following calendar month. Member Firms are required to make any appropriate changes to the way in which they are representing such orders within five days after the end of each calendar month. This amendment became effective July 1, 2026.

Please contact rmteam@nyse.com with any questions about this update.

data.subject: NYSE Arca: Fee Changes Effective September 2026 - Retail Remove Modifications
data.body:
Beginning September 1, 2026, NYSE Arca will modify the definition of certain Retail Orders that remove liquidity for clients at the Retail Tiers, pending effectiveness of a regulatory filing. 

ETP Holders qualifying for Retail Tiers 1, 2, 3, 5, and 6 will be subject to a new condition requiring a time-in-force of Day for Retail Orders where each side of the executed order shares the same MPID. The current rate of no fee or credit continues to apply to orders meeting these criteria. 

Additionally, the definition of Retail Removing Orders with a time-in-force of Day for the Tiered Remove rates will be modified to exclude Retail MPL Orders and Retail Discretionary Pegged Orders that remove liquidity. The Remove Rates and Caps for Retail Tiers 1, 2, 3, 5, and 6 remain unchanged.

data.subject: NYSE Arca: Extended Hours Trading Effective December 6, 2026 - Update
data.body:
Beginning Sunday, December 6, 2026, NYSE Arca will operate 23 hours a day, with an Overnight Session beginning at 9:00 PM ET on Sunday through Thursday evenings and ending at 8:00 PM ET the following day, as previously announced.

Updated Order Entry Specifications

  • NYSE Pillar Binary Gateway Specification
  • NYSE Pillar FIX Gateway Specification

Market data specifications will be published at a later date.

Testing

The Exchange will conduct six tests ahead of the December 6 Production launch, in conjunction with the Securities Information Processors. Tests will begin at 11:00 PM on Friday and conclude at 12:00 PM on Saturday.

The scheduled industry test dates are:

  • October 2 | October 16 | October 30 | November 6 | November 20 | December 4

Beginning November 8, 2026, test symbols will be available for Production testing during the Overnight Session.

 

For additional information, visit nyse.com/extended-hours-trading or review the updated Extended Hours Trading Frequently Asked Questions. 

Please contact rmteam@nyse.com with questions about these updates.

data.subject: NYSE American Options: Extended Trading Hours - Update
data.body:
Overview

NYSE American Options will introduce Extended Trading Hours ("ETH") for certain eligible equity options, as previously announced.

Two new sessions will be added before and after the Core Trading Session: an Early Trading Session from 7:30 AM to 9:25 AM ET and a Late Trading Session from 4:00 PM to 4:15 PM ET. The Core Trading Session will remain unchanged.

Updates

  • Certification Testing will be available beginning Tuesday, August 18, 2026
    • Available Symbols: AAPL, AMD, AMZN, AVGO, BABA, BAC, F, GLD, GOOG, GOOGL, HOOD, INTC, IWM, META, MRVL, MSFT, MU, NFLX, NOK, NVDA, ORCL, PFE, PLTR, QQQ, SNDK, SPY, TSLA, TSM, XLF. 
      • GLD, IWM, QQQ, SPY, XLF will be available for the Core Trading Session (Session 2) until 4:15 PM, not in the Late Trading Session (Session 3).
    • Including Early and Late Trading Sessions
  • Test Symbols available in Production beginning Monday, September 21, 2026 will be NTEST (enabled for Early, Core, Late) and PTEST (enabled for Early, Core).
  • The NYSE American Options Extended Trading Hours Fact Sheet has been updated.

 

Please contact rmteam@nyse.com with questions about this update.

data.subject: NYSE Group - Auction Reference Price Changes
data.body:
Overview

Beginning August 31, 2026, NYSE, NYSE American, NYSE Arca, and NYSE Texas will update the reference price calculation for the Core Open Auction and NYSE will also modify its Trading Halt Auction to incorporate the last consolidated trade of at least one round lot of that trading day. 

Core Open Auction Reference Price Changes

The Opening Reference Price will be calculated using the following hierarchy:

  1. The price of the last consolidated trade of at least one round lot, excluding early and late session trades that originated from a Trade Reporting Facilities (TRF), or
  2. If no such trades occurred, the midpoint of the Auction NBBO, or
  3. If the Auction NBBO is locked, the locked price, or
  4. If there is no Auction NBBO, the prior trading day's Official Closing Price for the initial calculation; for each subsequent calculation, the most recently calculated Opening Reference Price.

NYSE Trading Halt Auction Reference Price Change

The NYSE Trading Halt Auction Reference Price will be calculated using the following hierarchy:

  1. The price of the previous, round lot, consolidated trade, excluding early and late session trades that originated from a TRF, or 
  2. Prior trading day's Official Closing Price.

Testing Opportunity

NYSE and NYSE Arca will offer a test on Saturday, August 22, 2026, to test the new reference price calculations.  Opening auctions will begin at 9:30 AM.
Implementation Schedule

data.subject: NYSE Group - Trading Halt Rules Update - Reminder and Revised Implementation Schedule
data.body:
Beginning August 10, 2026, NYSE Group equities exchanges will implement certain previously approved amendments to their trading halt rules. These changes are the result of coordinated work by the NYSE Group and the other SROs to establish common criteria and procedures for resuming trading in equity securities when regulatory or operational issues arise. 

Trading Halt Rules Updates

  • Clarify the situations that allow a Primary Listing Market to declare a Regulatory Halt: (1) as provided by the SIP Plans, (2) discretionary Regulatory Halts, and (3) mandatory Regulatory Halts;
  • Provide detailed and consistent rules on how a Primary Listing Market will initiate halts and resume trading in the event of a Regulatory Halt and specify the obligations of other exchanges under the circumstances; and
  • Clarify the discretion afforded to the NYSE Group exchanges to impose an Operational Halt that applies only to that exchange's market.

The updated rules may be found in the Exchanges' rulebooks beneath the current versions of Rules 7.18 / 7.18E / 7.18-E.

Industry Test

NYSE and NYSE American will participate in an industry test on Saturday, August 8, 2026, to test the implementation and repurposing of certain Reason Halt Codes (specifically, "A," "F," "V," and "X"). A test script for the August 8th test can be found here.

data.subject: NYSE American Options: Extended Trading Hours
data.body:
Overview

NYSE American Options will introduce Extended Trading Hours ("ETH") for certain eligible equity options. Two new sessions will be added before and after the Core Trading Session: an Early Trading Session from 7:30 AM to 9:25 AM ET and a Late Trading Session from 4:00 PM to 4:15 PM ET. The Core Trading Session will remain unchanged.

Implementation Schedule

  • Certification Testing Available: Friday, August 14, 2026 
  • Pre-Production with Test Symbols: Monday, September 21, 2026 
  • Production Symbols: To be announced via a subsequent Trader Update, pending effectiveness of regulatory filings (will go live no earlier than September 21, 2026)

Participation Requirements

To participate in ETH, firms must have a Letter of Guarantee from a Clearing Member authorized by the OCC and provide appropriate risk disclosures to customers before accepting orders. Firms may use their existing NYSE Pillar gateway ports with a new TradingSessionID value to participate.

Updated System and Proprietary Market Data Specifications

  • NYSE Pillar Binary Gateway Specification
  • NYSE Pillar FIX Gateway Specification
  • NYSE Pillar Binary Gateway Order Type Matrix
  • NYSE Pillar FIX Gateway Order Type Matrix
  • Options Top Client Specification
  • Options Deep Client Specification
  • NYSE Pillar Options Common Client Specification
  • NYSE Options Open-Close Volume Summary
  • NYSE Pillar Equities Common Client Specification

Market Data changes will also be reflected in the NYSE American Options and NYSE Arca Options Symbol Mapping files available here.

 

For additional information, please review the NYSE American Options Extended Trading Hours Fact Sheet. Please contact rmteam@nyse.com with questions about this update.

data.subject: NYSE Arca - Extended Hours Trading Effective December 6, 2026
data.body:
Beginning Sunday, December 6, 2026, NYSE Arca will operate 23 hours a day. An Overnight Session will begin at 9:00 PM each evening, Sunday through Thursday, and end at 8:00 PM the following day. If a US exchange holiday falls between Monday and Friday, the Exchange will conclude its Late Session trading the evening before the holiday. The next Overnight Session will begin at 9:00 PM the evening of the holiday, if the following day is a trading day. All times are ET.

NYSE Arca Extended Trading Hours Functionality

  • New Trading Session: An Overnight Session will be introduced as a fourth distinct session on the existing NYSE Arca platform, covering all NMS securities from 9:00 PM to 4:00 AM. The Overnight Session will open with continuous trading at 9:00 PM with no opening auction; order entry will open at 8:59 PM. The existing Early, Core and Late Sessions will not change.
  • Connectivity: Firms will use their existing NYSE Pillar Gateway ports and submit a new TradingSessionID value to participate in the Overnight Session. 
  • Risk Controls: Existing risk limits (e.g., Gross Credit) will be available in the Overnight Session as in all other sessions. In addition, Entering and Clearing firms may opt clients in or out of the Overnight Session at the MPID or MPID + SubID level. 
  • Order Protection: Clearly Erroneous Execution (CEE) protections will be extended to the Overnight Session with doubled numerical guidelines. Limit Order Price Protection will apply as in the Early and Late Sessions.
  • Market Data: Consolidated and NYSE Arca proprietary data feeds will be available throughout the extended operating schedule on existing publication channels. A new Security Status message value of 'n' will be added for the Overnight Session in the Security Status and Market State fields. 
  • Specifications: Updated system specifications will be distributed via Trader Update in August.

Testing

In conjunction with the Securities Information Processors, the Exchange will conduct six tests ahead of the December 6 Production launch. Tests will begin at 11:00 PM on Friday and conclude at 12:00 PM on Saturday. The scheduled industry test dates are:

  • October 2 | October 16 | October 30 | November 6 | November 20 | December 4

Beginning November 8, 2026, NYSE Arca will support trading of test symbols in Production during the Overnight Session.

Regulatory Updates

  • LULD Plan Amendment: The LULD Plan has filed an amendment with the SEC to create Overnight Price Bands, which would be in effect from 9:00 PM to 4:00 AM, calculated using two reference prices: the primary listing market's official closing price and the consolidated last round lot sale as of 7:45 PM. NYSE Arca is prepared to implement these changes if the SEC approves the LULD Plan amendment.
    • The lower band would be set 20% below the lower reference price; the upper band would be set 20% above the higher reference price. 
    • Unlike LULD Bands in the Core Session, limit states would not be calculated by the SIPs and there would be no automatic Trading Pauses. Primary Listing Markets would instead have discretion to declare a Regulatory Halt for the remainder of the Overnight Session. 
  • Corporate Actions: The primary listing markets have agreed on harmonized rules for mandatory Regulatory Halts affecting securities subject to certain corporate actions. These rules will provide exchanges and market participants adequate time to process complex corporate actions and make adjustments to systems, orders, quotes, and reference data. For details, see the Corporate Action Halt Rules FAQ.


For additional information, visit nyse.com/extended-hours-trading or review the Extended Hours Trading FAQs.  Please contact rmteam@nyse.com with questions about these updates.

data.subject: NYSE Group: Market Wide Circuit Breaker Test July 25, 2026
data.body:
On Saturday, July 25, 2026, NYSE, NYSE American, NYSE Arca, NYSE National and NYSE Texas will participate in the Securities Information Processors' (SIPs) industry testing of Market-Wide Circuit Breaker (MWCB) Level 1 and 2. NYSE Group equities markets will be available from their primary data sites in Mahwah from 9:30 a.m. to 12:00 p.m. ET.  

Designated required participants for the October 2026 Reg. SCI test on NYSE, NYSE American, NYSE Arca, NYSE National and NYSE Texas are required to participate in at least one MWCB test, per year.  Firms required to test have been notified of their requirement.  

The script for the test can be found here. The testing requirements below must be completed for each NYSE Group equities exchange for which the firm has been designated as a required tester:  

  • Receive and process MWCB halt messages from the SIPs.  
  • Receive and process resume messages from the SIPs following a MWCB halt.  
  • Receive and process market data from the SIPs relevant to the MWCB halt.  
  • Send orders following a Level 1 or Level 2 MWCB halt in a manner consistent with usual trading behavior.  

Firms should register to test at trading@nyse.com to have their participation recorded. Following the test, firms must return the participation checklist to Regscitesting@nyse.com.  

Remaining 2026 SIP Failover/MWCB Saturday Testing Dates  

  • July 25, 2026 - SIP Failover / MWCB Level 1/2 Test #2  
  • September 12, 2026 - MWCB Level 1/2/3 Test   
  • December 5, 2026 - SIP Failover / MWCB Level 1/2 Test #3

data.body:

Eligibility Requirements

To qualify, a security must meet the following criteria on a quarterly basis:

  • Individual stocks with a market capitalization exceeding $700 billion (based on closing price), or ETFs with Assets Under Management exceeding $50 billion (based on net asset value)
  • Monthly options volume exceeding 10 million contracts in the final month of the preceding quarter
  • A position limit of at least 250,000 contracts

data.subject: NYSE Options - July 2026 Fee Changes
data.body:
Effective July 1, 2026, NYSE Options will adopt the following fee changes:

  • Introduce an MM/LMM Posting Incentive Program for Designated Non-Penny Issues on NYSE Arca Options, pending effectiveness of a regulatory filing.
  • Implement a new methodology for determining Options Regulatory Fees ("ORF") and modify rates to $0.0160 on NYSE American Options and $0.0120 on NYSE Arca Options, as previously announced.

Market Maker Posting Incentive Program for Designated Non-Penny Issues

Under the new program, Market Makers are eligible to receive an additional $0.40 per contract credit on top of the base $0.05 MM and $0.40 LMM Non-Penny Post Liquidity credits, when the combined rate is higher than the applicable credit under the existing Non-Customer, Non-Penny Posting Credit Tiers.

This program will apply to new listings that trade more than 1 million contracts in industry volume, as reported by OCC, on their first day of listing, and will remain in effect until the symbol is added to the Penny Interval Program.

data.subject: NYSE, NYSE Arca - Updated Limit Up Limit Down Tier 1 ETP List July 2026
data.body:
NYSE Arca and NYSE, in coordination with other listing exchanges, have updated the list of Exchange Traded Products eligible for Tier 1 of the Limit Up Limit Down ("LULD") program, effective July 1, 2026.

The updated list of ETPs, along with the additions and deletions from the current Tier 1 list, can be found here.

Tier 1 Eligibility Criteria

To determine eligibility as a Tier 1 NMS stock, all ETPs across multiple asset classes and issuers were sorted by notional consolidated average daily volume ("CADV"). The list includes domestic equity, international equity, fixed income, currency, and commodities and futures but excludes leveraged ETPs. Notional CADV was calculated by multiplying daily volumes by closing prices each day of the measurement period and then averaging them for the period. The measurement period was the first day of the previous fiscal half year up until one week before the beginning of the next fiscal half year, in this case, January 2, 2026 to June 24, 2026. ETPs, including inverse ETPs, that traded over $2,000,000 CADV were eligible to be included as a Tier 1 NMS stock.

Please contact rmteam@nyse.com with any questions about this update.

data.subject: NYSE Group - Trading Halt Rules Updates
data.body:
NYSE Group equities will implement changes to its Trading Halt Rules as outlined below.

Trading Halt Rules Update

Beginning August 10, 2026, NYSE Group will adopt updated Trading Halt rules that provide for the following changes:

  • Reorganize existing halt authority and resumption procedures
  • Provide the exchanges with discretion to halt trading in the event of a SIP Outage, Material SIP Latency, or Extraordinary Market Activity
  • Specify rules for Operational Halts that apply to only one market

The updated rules may be found in the exchanges' rulebooks beneath the current versions of Rules 7.18 / 7.18E / 7.18-E.

Production Implementation Schedule

Market

Date

NYSE, NYSE American - Industry Test*

Saturday, August 8, 2026

NYSE American

Monday, August 10, 2026

NYSE Arca, NYSE National

Tuesday, August 11, 2026

NYSE, NYSE Texas

Thursday, August 13, 2026

* A test script for the industry test will be distributed prior to the test.

 

Corporate Action Regulatory Halts

In support of 23/5 Trading, NYSE Arca has filed with the SEC rules for mandatory regulatory halts for securities subject to certain corporate actions.  These rules ensure that both the Exchange and market participants have adequate time to process complex corporate actions and make the necessary adjustments to systems, orders, quotes and reference data.  

These rules will become effective upon the launch of 23/5 Trading in December 2026. For further information, refer to the Corporate Actions Halts FAQ.

 

Please contact rmteam@nyse.com with any questions about these updates.

data.subject: NYSE - 2026 Russell Reconstitution
data.body:
Russell Reconstitution - June 26, 2026 

Overview 

The newly reconstituted Russell indices (Russell Global Index, Russell 1000® Index, Russell 2000® Index Russell 3000® Index and Russell Microcap® Index) will take effect on Monday, June 29, 2026, and will remain in place for the next 6-months. The previous indices will cease being in effect after the close of the U.S. equity markets on Friday, June 26, 2026. FTSE Russell will use the NYSE Official Closing Prices to price NYSE-listed securities added to the indices.  

Please review the FTSE Russell webpage for updates and final lists of additions and deletions. 

Normal Market on Close/Limit on Close (MOC/LOC) rules and procedures will apply on June 26, 2026. 

The NYSE would like to remind participants of various system interruption contingencies as we head into the Russell Reconstitution. 

Communications 

NYSE will use its standard system status communication methods - www.nyse.com/market-status/history, SMS and email - to disseminate event updates and inform market participants of any unusual market conditions. To subscribe or update preferences for NYSE Market Status Notices, visit www.nyse.com/subscriptions. 

Contingency Procedures 

If the NYSE experiences a system disruption that would impact its ability to conduct a closing auction, it will execute one of the following contingency scenarios:  

System Interruption Contingency Scenario 1 (At or Before 3:00 PM) 

If after exhausting all recovery options, the NYSE determines at or before 3:00 p.m. ET that it is unable to conduct a closing transaction in one or more securities, the NYSE will designate NYSE Arca as the alternate exchange. Consequently, the NYSE's Official Closing Price in the affected securities will be the official closing price under the rules of NYSE Arca. In such an event, all closing interest on the NYSE in the affected securities will be deemed cancelled and member organizations will be encouraged to re-route their closing interest for participation in the NYSE Arca closing process. 

System Interruption Contingency Scenario 2 (After 3:00PM) 

If an NYSE system interruption occurs after 3:00 p.m. ET whereby service will not be restored, the NYSE's Official Closing Price will be the VWAP of the last consolidated sale prices for the last five minutes of trading for each affected NYSE-listed security. The NYSE will notify market participants via the market-wide call and a system status posting that the closing process will not occur and that all closing interest on the NYSE in the affected securities will be deemed cancelled. 

Questions about this memo should be directed to your Relationship Manager or rmteam@nyse.com.

data.subject: NYSE Arca - Extended Hours Trading Effective December 6, 2026
data.body:
Beginning December 6, 2026, subject to SEC approvals, NYSE Arca will extend its trading hours to operate from 9:00 PM  ET Sunday through 8:00 PM ET Friday, with a one-hour pause between 8:00 PM and 9:00 PM ET Monday through Thursday, excluding holidays.  

Highlights 

New Trading Session - NYSE Arca will introduce the Overnight Trading Session as a fourth distinct session, running from 9:00 PM to 4:00 AM and trading all NMS securities. Trading begins continuously at 9:00 PM with no opening auction. Order entry will begin one minute earlier, at 8:59 PM.  

Existing Connectivity - Firms will use their existing NYSE Pillar Gateway ports and send a new TradingSessionID value to participate in the Overnight Session. Clearing firms can opt clients in or out of the new Overnight Session at the MPID level.    

Order Protection - NYSE Arca will extend Clearly Erroneous Execution (CEE) protections to the Overnight Session, with doubled numerical guidelines. Limit Order Price Protection will apply in the Overnight Session as in all other sessions. Additionally, the LULD committee has filed a proposed amendment to extend market-wide volatility controls to the Overnight Session. 

Corporate Action Processing - NYSE Arca and other listing exchanges will file rules to standardize how certain corporate actions are handled overnight, including the ability to declare regulatory halts uniformly across all NMS securities 

Market Data - Consolidated and NYSE Arca Proprietary Data Feeds will be available 23 hours a day. 

Updated system specifications will be distributed via Trader Update. 

For additional information, please visit NYSE Extended Hours Webpage or review the Extended Hours Trading Frequently Asked Questions.

data.subject: NYSE Arca Options - NYSE Pillar Hardware Upgrade – Final Reminder
data.body:
On Monday, June 1, 2026, NYSE Arca Options will upgrade hardware for its NYSE Pillar technology platform. There are no changes to specifications or sessions, and the migration will be an immediate cutover with no parallel production period, as previously announced.  

The Certification environment is currently available on the new hardware, and the final industry test is scheduled for Saturday, May 30, 2026. 

Proprietary Market Data Feeds  

Concurrently with the hardware upgrade, NYSE Arca Options Top (BBO and Trades), Deep and Complex (excluding Imbalance and Summary) feeds will expand from 17 to 24 Publisher, Refresh and Retransmission channels.  

Please note that Certification Source IPs will change and the NYSE Proprietary Data IP Addresses file has been updated to reflect new Production channels and Certification source IPs. 

Customers should use the start of day symbol reference data for symbol mapping information. There will be no XDP format changes.

Key Dates 

Industry Test  

Saturday, May 30, 2026 

New hardware in Production 

Monday, June 1, 2026 

Heartbeats on new market data channels

Test symbols on new market data channels

data.subject: NYSE Arca Options - NYSE Pillar Hardware Upgrade - Reminder
data.body:
On Monday, June 1, 2026, NYSE Arca Options will upgrade hardware for its NYSE Pillar technology platform. There are no changes to specifications or sessions, and the migration will be an immediate cutover with no parallel production period, as previously announced.  

The Certification environment is currently available on the new hardware and the first industry test is scheduled for Saturday, May 16, 2026. 

Proprietary Market Data Feeds  

Concurrently with the hardware upgrade, NYSE Arca Options Top (BBO and Trades), Deep and Complex (excluding Imbalance and Summary) feeds will expand from 17 to 24 Publisher, Refresh and Retransmission channels.  

Please note that Certification Source IPs will change and the NYSE Proprietary Data IP Addresses file has been updated to reflect new Production channels and Certification source IPs. 

Customers should use the start of day symbol reference data for symbol mapping information. There will be no XDP format changes. 

 

Key Dates 

Industry Test #1 

Saturday, May 16, 2026 

Industry Test #2

New hardware in Production 

Monday, June 1, 2026 

Heartbeats on new market data channels

Test symbols on new market data channels

data.subject: NYSE and NYSE Arca - Fee Changes Effective May 1, 2026
data.body:
Effective May 1, 2026, pending effectiveness of regulatory filings, NYSE and NYSE Arca will modify rates for securities with a per share price of $1.00 or above, as follows:

NYSE Arca - New Retail Tier 6

NYSE Arca will introduce new Retail Tier 6 for orders that meet the following requirements:

  • Retail Orders with a time-in-force of 'Day' that add and remove at least 0.075% of CADV; and
  • Option Customer and Professional Customer Electronic Posting Volume of TCADV by OTP Holder or OTP Firm affiliated with the ETP Holder of at least 1.00%.

ETP Holders that meet the above, will be eligible for the following rates:

  • $0.0035 Credit for Retail Adding; and
  • No fee for Retail Removing with a Time-in-force of Day up to a limit of 65 million shares, with a fee of $0.0025 for shares above that limit.

NYSE - Removal Of Step-Up Tiers

NYSE will eliminate Step-Up Tier 4 and Step-Up Tier 5 from its Price List.

  • Step Up Tier 4: Credit of $0.0015 for adding in Tape A Securities for qualifying member organizations 
  • Step Up Tier 5: Credits for qualifying member organization's market participant identifier ("MPID") as follows:
    • $0.0001 incremental credit for adding in Tape A Securities for an increase of at least 0.10% or a $0.0002 incremental credit for an increase of at least 0.175% over the Baseline Month.
    • $0.0029 credit for adding in Tape B and C Securities for an increase of at least 0.25% over the Baseline Month.

data.subject: NYSE American Options and NYSE Arca Options: MSCI Index Options Available for Trading on May 1, 2026 - MXUSA, MXWLD, MXACW
data.body:
Effective May 1, 2026, options on the MSCI USA Index (MXUSA), MSCI World Index (MXWLD), and MSCI ACWI Index (MXACW) will be listed on NYSE American Options and NYSE Arca Options - expanding the suite of global index options available to market participants. 

This addition builds on ICE's decades-long partnership with MSCI, which includes providing the world's most liquid MSCI futures markets and reflects a continued commitment to offering clients greater choice and flexibility across global benchmarks. 

For additional information, please visit the NYSE MSCI Global Index Options webpage or contact rmteam@nyse.com.
